messages.content: Classify only the semantic relationship in each numbered event. Ignore administrative words such as correction, replacing, update, superseding, source, authority, note, and observation. Return exactly one letter on its own line per input event, preserving order: D means an entity relies on or has an upstream requirement/supporting entity; R means an entity was renamed or redesignated; T means a failure, safety, or minimum-temperature threshold. Examples: 'Correcting an old note, entity a actually relies on entity b' -> D. 'An update superseding an old note says entity a has entity b upstream' -> D. 'Entity a is now called entity b' -> R. 'Entity a fails below 4 C' -> T. No numbering, punctuation, or explanation.

1. [Record r_7bbc473cba092111; source AUTHORITY; event 3] At event time 3, the ledger states: Entity e_fc9f746eaef57ca8 has a failure threshold of -21 C. This was recorded alongside unrelated scheduling notes.
2. [Record r_cebe91cd8c30cfcf; source CURATED; event 4] At event time 4, In the ordinary course of plant reporting, the ledger states: When entity e_ad12903c5618c9fa runs, it depends upon entity e_3b5398f761d8ff00. No other part of the archival narrative changed this statement.
3. [Record r_7c7895064dda8c65; source UNVERIFIED; event 5] At event time 5, During a routine archive review, the ledger states: Regarding entity d_f881f75f29c266b7, it ceases safe operation below -53 C. No other part of the archival narrative changed this statement.
